newsitem.title: USA: Transco says restoring NY natgas pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Transco says restoring NY natgas pipeline.

text.p: Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line (Transco) said it is repressurizing its natural gas pipeline on Staten Island, N.Y., after police removed a possible bomb from an area along the line.
"The bomb squad has taken the device away. We expect to be back on shortly," Transco spokesman Chris Stockton said.

Indeed an official at the New York Police Department spokesman's office said that "the device was safely removed at 2:07 p.m. (1407 EST/1907 GMT). "It has been taken to (a nearby) police facility to determine if it was a bomb."
Buckeye Pipeline Co's spokesman meanwhile said Buckeye expected to restart its two parallel 12-inch refined oil products lines momentarily.

"We expect to be given the go ahead to restart momentarily," said Buckeye spokesman Roy Haase, noting area residents have already been allowed to return to their homes. Buckeye shut down the line earlier Wednesday, he said.
Transco's Stockton said it would only take about 15 minutes to bring pressure in the 26-inch diameter line back up to normal, or about 600 pounds per square inch (psi).
Transco cut the line's pressure to about 60 psi earlier Wednesday as a precaution after what police called a "suspicious package" had been found along the line.
Stockton said he had no further information on whether the package had, in fact, been a bomb.
Transco's line runs from Staten Island north, across the entrance to New York harbor, to Brooklyn where it feeds into Brooklyn Union's local natural gas delivery system.

The downed Buckeye section transports jet fuel to New York City's two airports from Linden, New Jersey, and also carries products like gasoline and heating around the city and out onto Long Island east of New York City.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk 1 212 859 1633
